elements.text: If pain severe, give morphine 5-10mg IM, repeat 4-6 hourly until patient referred, or give diluted morphine1 3-10mg slow IV: start with 3mL IV over 3 minutes. If needed, give another 1mL/minute until pain improved, up to 10mL. Stop if BP drops < 90/60.

to 12 hourly.

• Apply bismuth subgallate compound ointment 6-12 hourly or insert bismuth subgallate compound suppositories into the rectum 3 hourly. • Also apply lidocaine 2% cream or amethocaine 1% before and after each bowel action.

Lump/pile Suspected worms Is worm flat and white with worm segments (blunt ended)?
• Advise and treat for constipation 60. • Advise to avoid straining. • If pile cannot be reduced or is thrombosed, refer.
Ulcer/s or perianal wart/s

• Refer if: warts inside vagina, on cervix or ano-rectal areas (especially if PLHIV or MSM), pregnant with large warts, warts numerous/ large/bleeding or infected. • Treat as for genital ulcer 65 or genital warts 68.
Tapeworm likely
Give albendazole 400mg daily for 3 days.

• If worm is thin and white, with anal itch worse at night, pinworm likely: give single dose mebendazole 100mg (and repeat dose after 2 weeks) or give single dose albendazole 400mg. • If other worm or unsure: give single dose mebendazole 500mg or single dose albendazole 400mg.

• Treat all household members at the same time. • Check Hb. If Hb < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man), anaemia likely 44. • Advise to avoid uncooked meat and use good hygiene: wash hands with soap and water before handling food/after using toilet, wash soiled clothing/bedding and dispose of faeces properly. Keep fingernails short and keep toilet seat clean. © dermnetnz.org
• Refer if: abdominal tenderness/pain, abdominal mass felt, vomiting, itchy red line under the skin that may move (larva migrans).

Approach to the patient with anal symptoms not needing urgent attention • If patient has anal sex, ask about genital symptoms and treat partner 62. If painless bleeding, passing mucus or unable to pass stools despite feeling the need to (tenesmus), treat for sexually transmitted proctitis: give single dose ceftriaxone 250mg IM2 and azithromycin 1g orally. If severe penicillin allergy3, omit ceftriaxone and increase azithromycin to 2g. If diarrhoea 58. • Then examine anal area to look for cause:
Red/raw skin

• Advise good hygiene. • Look for contact cause. If diarrhoea 58. • Wash with aqueous cream (UEA), avoid soap. • Apply zinc and castor oil ointment to raw areas. If severe itching, also apply hydrocortisone 1% cream twice a day for 5 days.
If no better with treatment, refer.
